text: The number one thing that's stopping you from becoming who you want to be is how much you

emphasize the end goal. And as somebody who has studied neuroplasticity, I can tell you that this shows up in three different ways. Number one is worrying about how long it's going to take. Number two is worrying that it's too late. And number three, worrying that the goal is so big that it feels unattainable. All three keep your brain focused on the gap, and your brain perceives that gap as a threat. Therefore, cortisol rises, motivation drops, and all of a sudden you've stopped before you even started when you learn that the brain only cares about repetition you learn to put one
foot in front of the other day in and day out and just focus on the
next step instead of the end goal that is when your entire life changes
